alternate_titles: The Gospel of St. Matthew in Tangkhul Naga (1907)
publisher: British and Foreign Bible Society, Calcutta / Baptist Mission Press

notes: 1907 landmark translation of the Gospel of Matthew into Ukhrul Tangkhul by Rev. William Pettigrew. Contains the complete Sermon on the Mount, the Lord's Prayer, and parables. Public Domain.

front_matter.title_page: Pa o Kamata Isha mai Jesu Christawui Khararchan: Matthew Kahona Kasa (1907)
front_matter.preface: The Gospel of St. Matthew was translated into the Tangkhul Naga language in Ukhrul between 1905 and 1907. Printed at the Baptist Mission Press, Calcutta, under the auspices of the British and Foreign Bible Society. It provides foundational examples of early Tangkhul theological orthography, honorific expressions, and didactic prose.

chapters.title: The Genealogy and Nativity of Christ (Matthew 1-2)
chapters.summary: The generational lineage and the arrival of the Wise Men in Bethlehem rendered in Tangkhul.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 1:18-21: Jesu Christawui kaphari hithada leisai: Awui ava Maryli Joseph eina phankahai ngachaoda maleiranglakha, ana Kazing Mangazing Katharawui eina phasa kapang theitserie. Chitharan awui va Josephna mikumo mashungna kahana, ali kakhana phasa maleiranglakha khangareili zanglaga kashang-phā eina thang-khavai ning khami leisai. Kala ana naomayār akha sashapra, kala nawui eina ali JESU hoda kahang sara, kasakei Ana awui mikumoli athumwui yorshi eina huikhui sara.
chapters.english_translation: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily. And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
grammar_notes: Causative verbal suffix '-shuk' or future volitional '-sara' (huikhui sara = shall redeem/save).
exercises: Identify the Tangkhul verb corresponding to 'espoused / betrothed'.
Explain the morphological derivation of 'huikhui' (to rescue/save).

chapters.title: The Lord's Prayer & The Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6)
chapters.summary: The classic Lord's Prayer (Ithui Kaphungli Kasa Ava) and ethical teachings on prayer and fasting.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 6:9-13: Chiwui vang nathumna hithada haikaphā salu: 'Ithui kazingramli kaphung Ava, Nawui ming katharaseru. Nawui ngashan kasakazing raseru. Nawui ningkazang kazingramli thada ngaleili ngasokalu. Ithuli tharan kashakhavai kachak zingsho zingsho ithuli milu. Kala ithumna ithuli kashikashili ngashankahaimi thada, ithuwui yorshili ngashankahaimilu. Kala ithuli kakhayangli makaso-alu, kashikashili huikhuilu; kasakei ngashankasakazing, kala pangashan, kala phashan chinawui kuppup thotli nawuisai. Amen.'
chapters.english_translation: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
grammar_notes: Direct imperative suffix '-lu' on verbal stems: salu (do/pray!), milu (give!), huikhuilu (deliver!).
Prohibitive negative imperative: 'ma-...-alu' in 'makaso-alu' (do not lead!).
exercises: Recite the Lord's Prayer in Tangkhul from memory.

chapters.title: Parables of the Kingdom of Heaven (Matthew 13)
chapters.summary: The Parable of the Sower and the Pearl of Great Price in rural agricultural Tangkhul imagery.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 13:3-8: 'Theilu, kachit kasana chitchikhavai vaye. Kala ana chitkhalangli, charakha shongzali tuksangie, kala vanaona rarlaga shaksangserie. Charakha ngalung thotli tuksangie, chithuili ngalei kachung malei; kala ngalei maleiranglakha khangateili phayokaserie. Kha zinga rar-daran chi meiratsangie, kala ngari maleimana chiwui vang kangsangserie. Charakha suh thotli tuksangie, kala suhna shoklaga pomsangserie. Kha charakha ngalei kaphāli tuksangie, kala theirarlaga akha eina thakharā, akha eina tharuk-magā, akha eina magā thotna.'
chapters.english_translation: Behold, a sower went forth to sow; And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.
grammar_notes: Multiplication idioms: 'akha eina thakharā' (one producing a hundredfold).
exercises: How does the Tangkhul translation convey the four types of soil?
What verb root expresses 'to wither away'?

chapters.title: The Golden Rule & The Narrow Gate (Matthew 7)
chapters.summary: Practical ethical guidance: judging others, seeking wisdom, and the narrow gate to life.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 7:7-14: 'Hanglu, chitharan nathumli misara; khayorlu, chitharan nathumna phāsara; shimkakhong kakorlu, chitharan nathumli hungkahang misara. Kachikathāna hangkakhui thapup khuiye; kala khayorkakhui thapup phāye; kala kakorkakhuili hungkahang miye. Khong kakatli zanglu; kasakei khong khangashir kala shongfa kakhangashir china kashili vashukana, kala zangkakhui bing kachungsai. Kha khong kakat kala shongfa kaphā china ringkaphali vashukana, kala chichi phākakhui bing kachamlakna.'
chapters.english_translation: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened. Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

vocabulary.meaning: to knock, rap on the gate

grammar_notes: Correlative paired clauses: 'hanglu... misara' (ask... it shall be given).
exercises: Translate Matthew 7:12 (The Golden Rule) into written Tangkhul.
Identify the imperative markers used in the exhortation.

chapters.title: The Transfiguration & Healing (Matthew 17)
chapters.summary: Christ's transfiguration on the high mountain and the healing of the afflicted youth.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 17:1-5: Zing kum tharuk ngaphalaga, Jesuna Peter, James, kala awui khanao Johnli kaphung kashang akhali athum kacham eina thukpingsangie. Kala athum mik-ngalemli Awui aphasa khangatei thotna: Awui mai zingkhamathān katha thada ngashangie, kala Awui kachon mangashan katha thada kachak-ngayei thotna. Kala theilu, athumli Moses kala Elijah tui-hanglakha theiserie.
chapters.english_translation: And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light. And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
grammar_notes: Temporal sequential conjunction: 'zing kum tharuk ngaphalaga' (after six days had passed).
Color and radiance descriptive compound: 'kachak-ngayei' (radiantly white).
exercises: Discuss the cultural significance of 'kaphung' in Tangkhul geography and cosmology.
Identify the names of the three disciples in Tangkhul orthography.

chapters.title: The Great Commission & Epilogue (Matthew 28)
chapters.summary: The resurrection, triumph over death, and the universal apostolic commission.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Matthew 28:18-20: Kala Jesuna athum ngalemli rarlaga hangmi: 'Kazingram kala ngaleili pangashan kuppup ili miserie. Chiwui vang nathumna valaga mikumo ngashan pupup-li tuitam kasalu, Avawui, Naomayārwui, kala Kazing Mangazing Katharawui ming eina athumli baptism milu. Kala I nathumli sakasashikahai ot pupupli shurkhavai tuitam kasalu: kala theilu, I thotwui kashikhavai thada zingsho pupup nathum eina li-leisara. Amen.'
chapters.english_translation: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

vocabulary.meaning: end of the age, consummation of time

grammar_notes: Universal quantifier 'pupup' attached to nominals (ngashan pupup = all nations; ot pupup = all commands).
Continuous presence promise marked by future auxiliary: 'li-leisara' (shall continuously abide).
exercises: Examine how Pettigrew rendered the Trinitarian formula into Tangkhul.
Translate the Great Commission into modern Standard Tangkhul.

pages.english_translation: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

lines: * mikumo ngashan (noun): all nations, diverse tribes, humankind
